Table 3.  The tensor order.  k = Q_5(sqrt 5), R = O (x)_{Z_5} O in O x O.  [S]+[P]
          [IUT4, Prop. 1.1, Prop. 1.4(iii)].
          R = {(u,v) in O^2 : u = v mod pi}, so [O^2 : R] = |O/pi| = 5, and
          dim_{Q_5}(k x k) = 4.  (O^2 is a Z_5-module, not a Q_5 vector space;
          the ambient Q_5-space is k x k, of dimension 4.)
      det of the transition matrix = -20,  v_5 = 1,  index 5,
      dim 4,  mu(R)/log5 = -1/4
    -> treating the tensor order as its own normalization loses exactly log5/4.
4:
Table 4.  The floor.  [S]+[P]
          [IUT4, Prop. 1.4(iii)] passes from the container to the smooth bound
          by -floor(A) <= -A + 1, so the slack is 1 + floor(A) - A.  In the
          moderate tame model here d_I + a_I = |I| is an integer, so it is
            1 + floor(lambda) - lambda.
          CORRECTION 2026-09-07 (round 2): an earlier version used
          ceil(lambda) - lambda.  The two agree off the integers and differ
          ON them: at lambda = 3 and 4 the slack is 1, not 0.
      lambda        1 + floor - lambda      ceil - lambda (wrong)
               3                     1                        0
         472/157               156/157                  156/157
         627/157                 1/157                    1/157
               4                     1                        0
    -> at lambda = 472/157 the slack is 156/157, and the entry margin of that
       same curve is 1/157.  Their RATIO is 156; they are not comparable in
       kind either -- one is a defect between a container and a smooth bound,
       the other a margin between the two sides of a comparison.

9:
Table 9.  An ideal gcd is not a norm gcd.  pi = 16+3sqrt5, N = 110, p = 661.
          [P]  661 splits; sqrt5 has the two roots 115 and 546 there.  Reducing
          a = (16+3 sqrt5)^110 and t = 1 - a + a^2 at each root shows that the
          661-factor of the numerator and that of the denominator sit at
          DIFFERENT primes, so cancelling total norms removes one too many.
      sqrt5 mod 661   a mod 661   v(1-a)   v(t), t = 1-a+a^2
              115           1        1                  0
              546         365        0                  1
      height with the correct ideal gcd : 1174.636200642495
      height after cancelling norms     : 1168.1424468026432
      difference                        : 6.493753839852
      log 661                           : 6.493753839852
    -> the error is exactly log 661, and the reason is visible in the table:
       the two valuations never sit at the same prime, while the total norms
       carry 661 twice and cancel it once too often.

     201             1              0   0
